value.rationale: A recent frozen-Jacobian square-root refinement has a natural question: whether a strong matrix-order condition guaranteeing local linear attraction also protects intermediate positive-definite factors. The result proves global cone preservation/convergence in every commuting dimension yet gives an open, exact 2x2 noncommutative failure at the second step under the same strict order condition. This is a motivated structural boundary between spectral stability and cone invariance, relevant where intermediate roots feed SPD-sensitive downstream operations; it is not merely a numeric sign test. It does not claim a general practical failure rate.
